Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:42: When a person drinks water for his thirst, he should direct this intention, to remember God's miracles with us. And specifically "for his thirst," because when a person is thirsty, his stomach is inflamed with fire, which indicates judgment, and in his drinking the water it indicates that these are the waters of Chesed that extinguish the judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:43: Likewise, the blessing "Creator of many souls" carries this very same intention, remembering the miracles of Chesed — except that the blessing "shehakol" is general and "Creator of many souls" is particular, and the intent is "Creator of many souls and their deficiencies" — this creation is from the side of Chesed, for He creates what souls need, namely, sufficient provision, without which the world could not exist at all — like water, which is the life of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:44: In the first blessing the term "nihyah" [came to be] is used, and here "boreh" [creates] — both these actions are associated with Chesed: YaVaH [an alternate spelling with letters representing Yah] corresponds to "let there be light" (Genesis 1:3). And likewise regarding "creation" — it is known what is explained in the Tikkunim (133a), that "man of Beriah rides upon a lion"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:45: "Over all that He created, to give life to the soul of every living thing." "Over all" — although we explained that the miracles come from the side of Chesed, the intent is that they are revealed in Chesed, and Chesed in Tzaddik [Yesod]; but their source flows from even higher, and the proof is the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, which the Zohar explains (parashat Beshalach 52b) depends upon Atika [the Ancient One, i.e., Keter]. Therefore, after mentioning what Chesed created — namely, the provision without which existence is impossible — it then speaks of the performance of miracles, which are from above and are revealed through the waters of Chesed; this is "over all that He created, to give life."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:46: This is what the author of the passage began by saying: all the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel were performed only through water — meaning, the place of their revelation was through water — and therefore the first plague was through water, to show that all the other miracles to come would be revealed through it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:47: He said "over all that He created," using the word "al" [over/upon] in the manner of (Isaiah 58:14), "then you shall delight over the Lord [al Hashem]," which is explained in the Zohar (parashat Yitro 83a); "al Hashem" ["over the Lord"] literally means "above KoL MaH" — meaning, that which is above "KoL MaH"; from there He created to give life to the soul of every living thing, for from there is the life that gives being to souls. And because the matter is in a hidden place, it does not say "who creates, to give life" [present continuous], which would be a constantly ongoing action, but rather "what He created" [past] — for it is hidden above, in the concealed place, "the man of Beriah of the Supernal."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:48: In this several things are included. First, what the commentators explained, that "to give life to the soul of every living thing" refers to the extra delights, which flow from there, as it says "you shall delight over the Lord." So too, the miracles that give life to Israel come from there. And "the soul of every living thing" over which death has power is revived through the supernal flow. This also includes the delight of souls — the souls of the righteous in the World to Come — for each of the righteous is called "living," as it is said (II Samuel 23:20), "and Benayahu son of Yehoyada, son of a living man" — this is "to give life to the soul of every living thing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:49: This blessing was instituted over water in particular, because when a person remembers the lower Chesed that is constantly present — namely water, or other things of delight that a person eats, all of which belong to the category of lower Chesed — he will then remember the supernal Chesed that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to perform in the future; and this is "over all that He created" — which explains that there is the wondrous delight, and likewise what He has already done regarding the miracles — and through this one clings to His love as is fitting.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:50: At the end of the blessing, which we say, "blessed is the Life of the worlds," one may understand what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Zohar, parashat Toldot Yitzchak, end of p. 135), where he says, regarding the Righteous One [Tzaddik/Yesod] who is called "Life of the worlds," in these words: "he is life in two worlds — above, which is the supernal world; and life toward the lower world, and the lower world exists and shines on his account." — end of quotation. It may be said that the two kinds of flow we mentioned — the first, the flow of sustenance, and the second, the flow of delight and miracles — are the two worlds explained in the passage; understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:51: Further, what showed us His love, blessed be He, was the descent of the manna, as it says in Tanchuma (Beshalach [Buber]) on the verse (Exodus 16:4), "Behold, I will rain down for you" — this is what Scripture says (Job 36:31), "for by them He judges peoples; He gives food in abundance." These heavens — by them He judges the nations of the world; know this, for when the generation of the Flood sinned, He judged them through them, as it is said (Psalms 11:6), "He shall rain upon the wicked snares [of fire and brimstone]." The people of Sodom, when they sinned, He judged them through the heavens, as it is said (Genesis 19:24), "and the Lord rained upon Sodom," etc. Sisera, when he sinned, He judged him through the heavens, as it is said (Judges 5:20), "from heaven they fought." "He gives food in abundance" — from them He gave sustenance to Israel, as it is said (Exodus 16:4), "Behold, I will rain down for you bread from heaven." A parable: to what is this comparable? To a baker standing by his oven — his enemy comes and he scoops up coals and puts them on his head; his friend comes and he takes out warm bread and gives it to him — the coals and the bread both came from the same oven. So the Holy One, blessed be He, brought down fire upon the Sodomites and burned them, and from the heavens He brought down manna for Israel. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject. They elaborated further there on the many miracles performed with the manna, and this suffices to arouse the heart to love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:52: Further, what showed the Holy One, blessed be He's, love for us was the giving of the Torah, as it says (Exodus 19:4), "You have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Me. And now, if you diligently listen to My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured possession [segulah] from among all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine." Our sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Mechilta: "you shall be to Me a treasured possession from among all the peoples" means that you shall be free for Me and engaged in the words of My Torah, and not engaged in other matters. "Segulah" — just as a person's treasure is precious to him, so you shall be precious to Me. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Karchah says: so as to fix this firmly in the ear — just as a wife is attached [meshugelet] to her husband, a son to his father, a servant to his master, a maidservant to her mistress — one might think you too are merely attached [in a dependent sense]; Scripture teaches, "for all the earth is Mine," and yet you shall be Mine, so to speak — I will not set or empower any other over you but Myself, and so it says (Psalms 121:4), "behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps." "A kingdom of priests" — I will not appoint over you any king from the nations of the world, and so it says (Song of Songs 6:9), "one is she, My dove." — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:53: The statement of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Karchah is understood together with Rashi's explanation of this verse, in these words: "segulah" — a cherished treasure, as in "and the treasure [segulat] of kings" — precious vessels and gemstones that kings hoard away — so shall you be to Me a treasure above the other nations. And do not say, "you alone are Mine and I have no others with you, and what more do I have that your dearness to Me be recognizable, since all the earth is Mine, and they are as nothing before Me and to Me" — rather, "you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests," that is, princes, as in (II Samuel 8:18), "and David's sons were priests [kohanim, i.e., chief ministers]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:54: He indicated the matter of love to us in saying "and you shall be to Me," which our sages, of blessed memory, explained as "I will not empower any but Myself over you." And similarly the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in parashat Vayikra (Zohar, parashat Vayikra 7b), in these words: happy are Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, did not give them over to any great one or agent — rather, Israel cling to Him and He clings to them, and out of His affection for them the Holy One, blessed be He, called them "servants" — this is what is written (Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me" — they are My servants. Afterward He called them "sons," this being what is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God." Afterward He called them "brothers," this being what is written (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and friends." Because He called them brothers, He wished to place His dwelling among them and not depart from them. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:55: Likewise, regarding the love shown in giving the Torah, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, admonished us in Mishneh Torah (Deuteronomy 4:32), "For ask now of the former days... has anything like this great thing ever happened, or has anything like it been heard? Has a people ever heard the voice of God [speaking]" — and he said (v. 36), "from heaven He made you hear His voice, to discipline you, and on earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire; and because He loved your fathers and chose his seed after him, and brought you out with His presence, with His great power, out of Egypt."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:56: Similarly, regarding the matter of love in the giving of the Torah to us (ibid. 4:38), "to drive out nations greater and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, to give you their land as an inheritance, as it is this day."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:57: On the matter of His love for us in the giving of the Torah, see what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, parashat Balak 192a) on the verse (Deuteronomy 33:2), "The Lord came from Sinai and shone forth from Seir," etc. — from there indicates the strength of His love, blessed be He, for us, like a father who loves his beloved son.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:58: On this aspect of love in the giving of the Torah, it says in the Mishnah (Avot 3:14): beloved are Israel, for a precious vessel by which the world was created was given to them, as it is said (Proverbs 4:2), "for I have given you good instruction," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:59: On the totality of the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed with us, we say in the Passover night Haggadah, "how much more so, doubled and redoubled, is the goodness that the Omnipresent has bestowed upon us — He brought us out of Egypt, He executed judgments upon them, He executed judgment on their gods, He slew their firstborn, He gave us their wealth, He split the sea for us, He brought us through it on dry land, He drowned our enemies in it, He gave us the Torah, He brought us into the land of Israel, and He built for us the Chosen House [the Temple]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:60: Likewise among the things that show the Holy One, blessed be He's, love for Israel is what a person contemplates in the order of prayer instituted for us by the Men of the Great Assembly. One of them is what we say every day in prayer: "with an everlasting love You have loved us, O Lord our God, with great and abundant compassion have You had compassion upon us" — and several particulars are mentioned in it that indicate His great love for us, and were we to elaborate on it we would depart from our purpose. In general they are: (1) "great and abundant compassion have You had compassion upon us" — this is a general statement encompassing all the aspects to be explained in the blessing. (2) "Our Father, for the sake of Your great Name" — meaning the Name shared with us. (3) "For the sake of our fathers who trusted in You." (4) "And You taught them the statutes of life." (5) "Our Father, merciful Father, have mercy upon us." (6) "And put understanding into our hearts" — that He placed in us intellect to understand more than the other nations. (7) "That we shall not be shamed nor humiliated nor stumble forever and ever" — namely forever, that is entirely long. (8) "Let us rejoice and be glad in Your salvation" — namely, "I am with him in distress" (Psalms 91:15). (9) "And break the yoke of the nations from our neck" — namely, the ingathering of exiles. (10) "For You are a God who performs salvations" — that He always performs salvations for the sustenance of the world, these being the five salvations explained in the Zohar at the beginning of parashat Bereishit (1a) and further in parashat Terumah. (11) "And You have chosen us from among every people and tongue" — namely (Deuteronomy 32:8), "when the Most High gave nations their inheritance, when He separated the children of man... for the Lord's portion is His people." (12) "And You have brought us near, our King, to Your great Name" — I heard from the mouth of my master, the honored Rabbi Isaac Luria Ashkenazi, that one must intend by this that He brought us near to His Name at the standing at Mount Sinai to give us the Torah, for the Torah and His great Name are all one, as explained in the Zohar in several places. (13) "To give thanks to You." (14) "To proclaim Your unity and to love You" — for AHaVaH [love] has the numerical value of ECHaD [one/unity], and there are thirteen kinds of love mentioned in this blessing, matching the numerical value of AHaVaH.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:61: Likewise, among the things that arouse love, we mention in the blessing "Emet Ve-yatziv" ["True and firm"]: "God of the world, our King, Rock of Jacob, shield of our salvation, for all generations; true it is that You are the Lord our God and the God of our fathers, our King, King of our fathers, our Redeemer, Redeemer of our fathers, our Rock, Rock of our salvation," etc., "You helped our fathers, You have been from the world a shield and savior to them and to their children" — and from here onward, all the words until "who redeemed Israel" — all of it indicates the Holy One, blessed be He's, love for us and the performing of several miracles, such as the Exodus from Egypt, the plague of the firstborn, the splitting of the sea, and the other particulars mentioned. If a person takes this to heart when reciting the blessing, and does not recite it as a rote command of men, surely his heart will be aroused with a great desire of love for the Holy One, blessed be He, and he will cling to Him while standing and praying before Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:62: Likewise in the blessing "Magen Avraham" ["Shield of Abraham"], which alludes to Chesed, everything we mention in it are kindnesses and actions of Chesed that arouse love: "God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob" — and we have already mentioned above this aspect regarding (Deuteronomy 10:15), "only your fathers did the Lord desire to love," etc., as explained above. "The great God, the supreme God, who bestows good kindnesses, who acquires all, and remembers the kindnesses of the fathers, and brings a redeemer," etc. — all these actions indicate the constancy of Chesed among the creatures without interruption: it does not say "He bestowed kindnesses" but "who bestows" [continuous present], for He bestows forever; likewise "acquires all" — it does not say "He acquired all" — and "remembers My kindnesses and brings a redeemer," but "acquires, remembers, and brings" — which surely indicates the constancy of the actions of Chesed. In the commentary on the prayers, each and every one of these actions will be explained as to how it indicates Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:63: Likewise in the blessing "Atah Gibor" ["You are mighty"], although it resembles Gevurah [severity], it is the sweetened Gevurah bound to Chesed — for we see that all the actions of Chesed are mentioned in it: "revives the dead, sustains the living with kindness, revives the dead with abundant mercy, supports the fallen, and heals the sick, and releases the bound, and fulfills His faithfulness" — and the matter of judgment is not mentioned explicitly except in the word "King who puts to death," and adjacent to it it says "and brings to life" — for even the matter of death, which is the harshest judgment, His intent, blessed be He, is for the good of man, in order to give him life, so that the world may emerge from its curses, and then "the Lord shall rejoice in His works." The particular matters mentioned in it several times regarding death and its other actions will be explained in the treatment of prayer. It follows that this blessing is the Gevurah bound to Chesed, and this is in the manner the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, parashat Ki Tissa 190b), which we quoted in chapter 1 of this Gate: that Abraham loves Isaac and Isaac loves Abraham, embracing one another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:64: Further, what we mention in the blessing "Modim" ["We give thanks"]: "for our lives, which are entrusted into Your hand, and for our souls, which are placed in Your charge, and for Your miracles that are with us every day" — "the Good One, for Your mercies never cease." And what we mention after our prayers, the thirteen attributes of mercy, "God, merciful and gracious," etc. — which indicate great kindness toward every person — should be examined carefully. Likewise, what we say on the Sabbath day, "had our mouths been full of song as the sea," etc., "from of old, from Egypt You redeemed us, O Lord our God; therefore, the limbs You have apportioned among us, and the breath and soul that You have breathed into our nostrils, and the tongue which You have set in our mouths," etc., "who saves the poor from one stronger than he — You shall hear the cry of the poor."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:65: Likewise what we say in the Grace after Meals, in the blessing "Nodeh" ["We give thanks"]: "for having given our fathers a desirable, good land," etc., "for having brought us out of the land of Egypt," "for Your covenant which You have sealed in our flesh" — this indicates the bond of love, that He, blessed be He, is bound with us, in that the sign of His Name is sealed in our flesh; and so it is the way of friends who love one another to make a bonded sign between them, as a token of their love that it never be forgotten. "For Your Torah which You have taught us" — explained above. And the matter of sustenance, too, is a sign of His kindness to all creatures.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:66: Likewise, when one remembers how many miracles were performed through the prophets — some through Samuel, some through Elijah, some through Elisha — he will recognize His greatness and goodness toward Israel. Beyond this are the miracles performed for Israel in every generation, which, were we to attempt to recount them, no book could contain them; this is what we say, that in every generation the idol-worshiping nations rise up against us to destroy us, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:67: All the miracles we have written, and several more we have not mentioned, are all recorded in the Book of Ezra [Nehemiah] (Nehemiah 9:6-28): "You alone are the Lord; You have made the heavens," etc., "You are the Lord God, who chose Abram," etc., "and You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt," etc., "and You split the sea before them," etc., "and with a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and with a pillar of fire by night, to give them light," etc., "and You came down upon Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them righteous ordinances," etc., "and You made known to them Your holy Sabbath," etc., "and bread from heaven You gave them for their hunger, and water from the rock You brought forth for them for their thirst, and You told them to go in to possess the land," etc., "but they and our fathers acted presumptuously and stiffened their necks," etc., "but You are a God of forgiveness, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in kindness, and You did not forsake them, even when they made themselves a molten calf," etc., "yet You, in Your abundant mercies, did not forsake them in the wilderness; the pillar of cloud did not depart from them by day," etc., "and You gave Your good spirit to instruct them, and Your manna You did not withhold from their mouths," etc., "forty years You sustained them in the wilderness, they lacked nothing; their clothes did not wear out," etc., "and You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and allotted them by portion, and multiplied their children as the stars of heaven," etc., "and they captured fortified cities and rich land, and took possession of houses full of every good thing," etc., "but they were disobedient and rebelled against You," etc., "and You gave them into the hand of their adversaries, who distressed them, and in the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You from heaven heard, and in Your abundant mercies You gave them saviors," etc., "and as soon as they had rest they turned again to do evil before You, and You abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, who dominated them; then they turned back and cried out to You, and You from heaven heard and delivered them, according to Your abundant mercies, many times." So too it is said in the Book of Judges (Judges 10:16), "and His soul was grieved for the misery of Israel" — see how great His affection for us, like a person distressed over his child's suffering.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:68: Further there, in Ezra [Nehemiah] (9:30-31): "and You bore with them for many years, and testified against them by Your spirit, through Your prophets, and yet they did not give ear," etc., "nevertheless, in Your abundant mercies You did not make an end of them, nor forsake them, for You are a gracious and merciful God" — end of quotation from the Book of Ezra.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:69: Further he should contemplate what our sages said in Tractate Avot (Avot 5:5): ten miracles were performed for our fathers in the Temple — no woman miscarried, etc. This was at the time the Temple stood, as a sign to Israel that the Shechinah dwelled among us; and as the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz wrote in Mishnat Boshet Panim, on the way to Gan Eden (there, ch. 20): may it be His will that the Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:70: Just as the Tabernacle was called "the Tabernacle of the Testimony," being a testimony to Israel that the Shechinah dwelled among them, so this reality was present in the Temple through the miracles performed there — particularly on Yom Kippur, with the scarlet thread that would turn white, to indicate whether "though your sins be like scarlet, they shall become white as snow," etc. (Isaiah 1:18).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:71: Even now, that it lies in ruins, this is a sign that it is because of our sins, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to build the Temple with His own hands — for when Israel left Egypt, His intent, blessed be He, was to bring down for us the Temple built above, had they not sinned with the calf; and so it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Pinchas 221a), in these words: when Israel left Egypt, the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to make them on earth like holy angels above, and wished to build for them a holy house and bring it down from within the heavenly heights, and to plant Israel a holy planting in the pattern of the supernal image; this is what is written (Exodus 15:17), "You shall bring them and plant them in the mountain of Your inheritance, the place, O Lord, which You have made for Your dwelling" — that which You, O Lord, made, and none other. "The place for Your dwelling which You have made" — this is the First Temple; "the Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established" — this is the Second Temple; and both of these are the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He. But since they angered Him in the wilderness and died, the Holy One, blessed be He, gathered [that intent] in to have it built by them in the land where their deeds had led them, and the house was built by human hands, and for this reason it did not endure. — end of quotation. And they elaborated further on this exposition there; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:72: Likewise, the miracle performed for all Israel in the days of Mordechai and Esther constituted the confirmation of the whole Torah, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat, chapter Ba-meh madlikin, 88a) — that at first, the mountain was suspended over them like a barrel, which serves as a great protest against [the validity of accepting] the Torah [under duress]; but in the days of Haman, "they confirmed and accepted" — they confirmed what they had already accepted, meaning they confirmed willingly and out of love what they had accepted under compulsion, since they saw how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for them, like a merciful father toward his son, whom the son is obligated to do the father's will [in return].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:73: You must know that all the miracles performed for us, and what is performed every day, and what will be performed, are all through the Shechinah, bound with us, she being the compassionate mother; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (17b): and because she is imprisoned with them in exile, it is said of her, "none imprisoned can free himself from prison," and the Shechinah is in her own house of imprisonment, for out of her love she is bound to them — and the secret of the matter is (Song of Songs 1:13), "a bundle of myrrh is my Beloved to me, between my breasts he lodges." And therefore whoever wishes to approach the King has no permission to approach Him except through the Shechinah — this is what is written (Jeremiah 9:22), "let not the wise man glory," etc., "but in this" [i.e., through her]. And Aaron, when he entered the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur, entered through her, as it is written (Leviticus 16:3), "with this [bezot] shall Aaron come into the sanctuary" — for it is a time for acting for the Lord. And Moses, through her, endures in the world — this is what is written (Deuteronomy 33:1), "and this [ve-zot] is the blessing with which he blessed." And through her he performed the ten plagues on Pharaoh — this is what is written (Exodus 9:16), "but for this [zot] purpose I have raised you up." And Jacob, because he knew that all the King's desire is in her, ordained for his sons that they should enter before the King only through her, and all their requests, prayers and supplications to the King should be through her — this is what is written (Genesis 49:28), "and this [ve-zot] is what their father spoke to them." And David, because he knew that all the King's desire and might and strength are in her, said (Psalms 27:3), "though [an army] should encamp against me," etc., "in this [be-zot] I trust" — for it is said of her (Psalms 103:19), "and His kingdom rules over all." Therefore, when Israel bring their petitions to the King, they say to her (Song of Songs 6:1), "whither has your Beloved turned, that we may seek him with you" — with several petitions of prayers and supplications, for it is because of you that he comes down to us and does not depart from us, except that we do not accord you honor, and for your sake he was bound with us all the six days [of the week]. — end of quotation. Here it is stated explicitly that the ten plagues were performed through her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:74: So too the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, parashat Ha'azinu 296b) regarding (Deuteronomy 32:6), "Is this how you repay [tigmelu zot] the Lord" — in these words: Rabbi Yehudah said: "Is this how you repay the Lord?" — because you are a crooked and perverse generation, you caused this — "zot" — to go into exile: "Is this how you repay the Lord?" — this is the repayment [gemul] that He performed for you in all those [ten] laws of Egypt, in all those signs He performed for you — this is the repayment with which you repay this? Who caused this to you? Because you are a base and unwise people, and you do not contemplate all the good He has done for you until now. "Is this how you repay the Lord?" — "zot" is the Shechinah, and we have already established this matter. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:75: So too it is explained in Shemot Rabbah, parashat "And Moses journeyed," etc. (24:1), on this verse, where the miracles are mentioned there, and as understood there, the two heh's — the Supernal Mother and the lower Mother — participated together in performing the miracles, in these words: "And Moses journeyed Israel," etc. — this is what is written, "Is this how you repay the Lord [ha-LaHashem tigmelu zot]?" — Rabbi Shisha, son of Rabbi Abba, would write the heh below and the lamed above [i.e., reading it as "Havu, ha-lo Hashem tigmelu zot" — "give heed, is it not that you repay the Lord thus"] — meaning, "take heed! Is this how you repay the Lord, this?" — after all the miracles He performed for you: that He split the sea into twelve openings for you, and drowned the Egyptians in the sea, His hand submerging them while His other hand saved you, as it is said (Exodus 15:6), "Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power; Your right hand, O Lord," etc., and He brought you up from the sea, and gave you their silver and gold, and everything upon their horses, which were adorned with silver and gold; and He fed you forty years, and did not leave you even a single hour — as many enemies came against you, He did not allow you to flee, but rather cast them down before you and guarded you — and not only from your enemies, but even from snakes and scorpions — and He gave you light before you, as it is said (ibid. 13:21), "and the Lord went before them by day" — have you forgotten all these miracles that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed with you, that the image of Micah was traveling with you, and you abandoned words of Torah and occupied yourselves with other matters? This is what is written, "Is this how you repay the Lord?" — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:76: Therefore it is fitting that we not be ungrateful for the good and the kindnesses we have received from Him, blessed be He, but rather strive to do His will and love Him just as He loves us; and we arouse the reality of this love in our prayers and commandments, in order to unify the Shechinah — for every unification is love, as explained above, and this is "and you shall love the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 6:5). Especially in this our exile, in which the union is separated and our Mother is in exile because of our sins, as it says (Isaiah 50:1), "and because of your transgressions your mother was sent away" — we must repair the union through our prayers and commandments; and this is like the parable of a loving son who asks his father for garments for his poor mother, and pleads with his father, weeping over her banishment, and reminds his father of the love of their youth, as it is said (ibid. 54:6), "and a wife of youth, when she is rejected" — and through this he arouses Tiferet's love for her, and the sons are obligated to arouse this love in their prayer. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (56, in the gloss): woe to those human beings whose hearts and eyes are sealed, who do not strive to know the honor of their Master, to appease Him through the Shechinah with several supplications and pleas, to bring Him down to the Shechinah — how much more so to arouse love in Him toward her — as they have instituted, "who chooses His people Israel with love." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:77: Further it is explained in the Tikkunim (35a) that the Shechinah is the one who guards us in every place, and therefore Israel is obligated to unify her in their commandments and their prayer, in these words: happy are Israel, who are constant companions to the Shechinah, standing with her both in ease and in distress — for when they are in judgment on the Day of Judgment, which is Rosh Hashanah, she stands with them in the judgment, since they stand for her in prayers, of whom it is said (Proverbs 6:22), "when you walk, it shall lead you; when you lie down, it shall watch over you; and when you awake, it shall talk with you" — for in every place Israel stand in every single commandment for the Shechinah, she stands for them in every hardship and distress, whether on the road, whether in settlement, whether at sea. This is "when you walk" through the desert, "it shall lead you" — this is what is written (Psalms 85:14), "righteousness shall go before Him, and shall set his footsteps on the way." "When you lie down" in settlement, "it shall watch over you"; "and when you awake" to descend to sea, "it shall talk with you." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:78: Now, of a kind with this love, the Rashbi, peace be upon him, said there (Zohar, parashat Ha'azinu, beginning of p. 298): it was taught, Rabbi Yehudah says: however much I have contemplated, the Holy One, blessed be He's, love for Israel has never departed from them, for wherever they are, the Holy One, blessed be He, is among them, as it is written (Leviticus 26:44), "I will not despise them, nor will I abhor them so as to destroy them, breaking My covenant with them" — precisely "with them," among them, with them — it never departs from them. Rabbi Yitzchak was traveling on the road and Rabbi Chiya met him; he said to him: I see in your face that your dwelling is in the dwelling of the Shechinah. What is written (Exodus 3:8), "and I have come down to save it from the hand of Egypt"? It should have said just "I have come down" — why "and I have come down," [implying "again"]? When did He first come down? When Jacob went down to Egypt. And why? "To save it from the hand of Egypt" — for were it not present among them, they could not have withstood the exile — meaning, "I am with him in distress; I will deliver him and honor him" (Psalms 91:15). He said to him: certainly, wherever Israel dwell, the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells among them. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:79: Further there: Rabbi Chiya said: it is written (Isaiah 49:15), "can a woman forget her nursing infant, that she should have no compassion on the son of her womb," etc. — this verse has already been explained, but what does it mean here? Come and see: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of his father: Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: since the day we fell into exile, the Holy One, blessed be He, has abandoned us in exile and forgotten us — this is what is written (Isaiah 49:14), "and Zion said, the Lord has forsaken me, and my Lord has forgotten me." The Shechinah said: "can a woman forget her nursing infant?" And are not Israel called sons, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God" — "the son of her womb," as it says (Jeremiah 2:21), "and I planted you a choice vine, wholly a seed of truth"? "Even these may forget" — as it is written (Genesis 2:4), "these are the generations of the heavens and the earth" — "but I will not forget you" — from here we learn that the Holy One, blessed be He, never abandons Israel. He said further: "can a woman forget her nursing infant, that she should have no compassion on the son of her womb" — this is a supernal secret which the Holy One, blessed be He, said, that these words are bound up in His Name, for just as the Holy One, blessed be He, does not forget His own Name, since it is His entirety, so the Holy One, blessed be He, does not forget Israel, who are bound up in His very Name. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:80: Since Israel are called sons and are bound up in His Name, it is fitting that they act as sons, in the manner of showing honor to their father; and so it is explained in the Midrash Devarim Rabbah, parashat Ki Tavo, on the verse "And Moses called all Israel," in these words: another interpretation (Proverbs 2:1), "My son, if you take my sayings" — Rabbi Yehudah bar Shalom said, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: when are you called My sons? When you take My sayings. To what may this be compared? To a king whose son said to him, distinguish me publicly throughout the kingdom, that I am your son. His father said to him: do you wish that all should know you are My son? Wear My purple robe and put My crown on your head, and all will know that you are My son. So too the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: do you wish to be distinguished as My sons? Engage in Torah and commandments, and all will see that you are My sons. — end of quotation. And what is meant by the metaphor of the purple robe and the crown: the purple robe is the commandments, which are a garment for the soul, and the crown is the Torah — and in its place we shall elaborate on the reason for this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:81: Further there: another interpretation — when are you My sons? When you take My sayings. Rabbi [Yehudah] said: when Israel were in the wilderness, the pillar of cloud went before them, and the smoke of the arrangement [of the altar] and the smoke of the incense would rise, and two sparks of fire would emerge from between the two staves of the Ark, burning before them the snakes and the scorpions; and the nations of the world would see them and say, these are divine beings, for all their use is only through fire. Moses said to them: and all this praise that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for you was because you accepted His Torah at Mount Sinai. Hence, "And Moses called all Israel and said to them" (Deuteronomy 29:1). — end of quotation.
